ColonyCouncil.TraitChangeDef.label: a psychopath made by executions, betrayal and loss

li.events: ExecutedPrisoner, ExecutedGuest, ExecutedColonist, ExecutedPrisonerGuilty, ExecutedPrisonerInnocent, HarvestedOrgan, HarvestedOrganFromGuest, HarvestedOrganFromColonist
li.label: carried out an execution or took an organ

ColonyCouncil.TraitChangeDef.meaning: {PAWN_nameDef} has done the colony's coldest work with {PAWN_possessive} own hands, more than once, after the people closest to {PAWN_objective} were lost or turned on {PAWN_objective}. Somewhere along the way {PAWN_pronoun} stopped feeling for anyone. It won't come back by itself.

plain.li: They looked at me oddly at supper. I couldn't think why. Then I remembered what I'd done, and I still couldn't.
I used to lie awake after an execution. Now I sleep fine.

warm.li: People keep telling me how sorry they are. I nod. I've learned when to nod.

blunt.li: Someone has to do it. I don't mind. That's the difference now.

cheerful.li: Everyone's been so tense lately. I can't think why. I feel fine.

gloomy.li: Whatever it was in me that hurt for other people, it's gone. I don't miss it. That should frighten me.

cold.li: Other people's feelings are a weather report now. I check them when it's useful.

ColonyCouncil.TraitChangeDef.label: a psychopath made by a long trail of killing

li.events: ExecutedPrisoner, ExecutedGuest, ExecutedColonist, ExecutedPrisonerGuilty, ExecutedPrisonerInnocent, HarvestedOrgan, HarvestedOrganFromGuest, HarvestedOrganFromColonist
li.label: carried out an execution or took an organ

ColonyCouncil.TraitChangeDef.meaning: Sixty lives and more have gone by {PAWN_nameDef}'s hand, and a grudge or a betrayal soured whatever feeling was left. Nothing will bring it back by itself.

plain.li: I've lost track of the faces. I haven't lost a night's sleep over any of them.
The others flinch at a death now and then. I watch them do it, like watching rain.

warm.li: I say the right words at funerals. I know them well by now. They don't mean anything going out.

blunt.li: They die, we live. It's that simple. It always was.

cheerful.li: I almost miss the raids when they stay away. An odd thing to miss, I suppose.

gloomy.li: Too many of them. Somewhere in the count I stopped being someone who minds.

cold.li: I have stopped weighing lives. It saves a great deal of time.

ColonyCouncil.TraitChangeDef.label: a cannibal made by famine

li.thoughts: AteHumanlikeMeatDirect, AteHumanlikeMeatAsIngredient, AteRawHumanlikeMeat, AteHumanMeat_Disapproved, AteHumanMeat_Horrible, AteHumanMeat_Abhorrent
li.label: ate human flesh while starving

ColonyCouncil.TraitChangeDef.meaning: Starving, {PAWN_pronoun} ate human flesh, and then again, and again. The horror of it has worn off, and what's left is a taste for it.

plain.li: The first time I was sick afterward. The third time I wasn't. I've been trying to decide what that means.
I catch myself thinking about that meat. Not with horror anymore.

warm.li: We did what we had to, to keep each other alive. I can't make myself regret it, or the taste.

blunt.li: Meat is meat. Hunger taught me that.

cheerful.li: I've stopped asking the cook what's in the stew. Lately I've started hoping.

gloomy.li: The famine's over. Whatever it did to me isn't.

cold.li: The taboo turned out to be only a taboo. The famine removed it.

ColonyCouncil.TraitChangeDef.label: a cannibal by faith and habit

li.label: ate human flesh as their ideoligion holds right

ColonyCouncil.TraitChangeDef.meaning: The faith {PAWN_nameDef} follows holds that human flesh is good to eat, and {PAWN_pronoun} has eaten it often enough now to want it for its own sake.

plain.li: The faith says it's right. My stomach agrees now, and it didn't use to.
I look forward to that meat now for its own sake. I didn't expect to admit that.

warm.li: We share the flesh as the faith asks, and I feel closer to everyone at the table for it.

blunt.li: I like it. The faith was right.

cheerful.li: Second helpings, please. The faith says it's good, and so does my stomach.

gloomy.li: I don't think I could go back to plain meat. I don't think I want to.

cold.li: Belief became habit, and habit became preference. A natural progression.
